input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 is the only non-solicit in the agreement and it fails every fallback element: it binds Customer only (not mutual), covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs eighteen months from termination rather than twelve months from the end of involvement, has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and by barring Customer from "engag[ing]" Vendor personnel operates as a no-hire — walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer "has made no ... no-hire commitment" and is free to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment". We therefore take the preferred position and replace the restriction with an express confirmation that Customer is not restricted, which also removes the internal conflict with 12.3.

proposal.summary: Replace the one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage with an express confirmation that Customer is under no such restriction.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the eighteen-month restriction because it bound only us, reached every person Vendor employed at any time during the term, extended to engagement (a no-hire), and had no general-advertising carve-out, and it contradicted Section 12.3's confirmation that we gave no no-hire commitment. If you need a covenant here, we can accept a mutual twelve-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring prohibition.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: Nothing in this Agreement restricts Customer from soliciting or engaging any person employed by Vendor.
